fact_text: Under accrual accounting a company can book sales it has not yet collected in cash, so operating cash flow can be far below reported revenue.

fact_text: EBIT is earnings before interest and taxes; it shows the margin from core operations as if the company carried no debt cost and paid no tax, and is divided by revenue to get the margin.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Profitability Ratios Explained | Part 07 |  Net Profit Margin, Gross Margin, EBIT, EBITDA, NIMs' (YouTube, 2026-03-14)

fact_text: EBITDA is EBIT with depreciation and amortisation added back; it is watched closely in capital-intensive businesses such as factories and large infrastructure operators.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Profitability Ratios Explained | Part 07 |  Net Profit Margin, Gross Margin, EBIT, EBITDA, NIMs' (YouTube, 2026-03-14)

fact_text: Margins should be tracked over several years; a sharp fall should be traced to an industry shock such as an oil price move or to company-specific problems before drawing a conclusion.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Profitability Ratios Explained | Part 07 |  Net Profit Margin, Gross Margin, EBIT, EBITDA, NIMs' (YouTube, 2026-03-14)

fact_text: Net interest margin is the net interest income a bank earns, divided by its total revenue in the analyst's method, and it is mainly used to compare banks with one another.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Profitability Ratios Explained | Part 07 |  Net Profit Margin, Gross Margin, EBIT, EBITDA, NIMs' (YouTube, 2026-03-14)

fact_text: A bank's net interest margin is the spread between the interest it earns on loans and the interest it pays on its own borrowing; the analyst's illustration of a 30% lending yield against a 20% borrowing cost gives a 10% spread.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Profitability Ratios Explained | Part 07 |  Net Profit Margin, Gross Margin, EBIT, EBITDA, NIMs' (YouTube, 2026-03-14)

fact_text: The cash flow statement splits a company's cash movements into operating, financing and investing activities, which shows where its cash comes from and where it goes.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Profitability Ratios Explained | Part 07 |  Net Profit Margin, Gross Margin, EBIT, EBITDA, NIMs' (YouTube, 2026-03-14)
